scenario: [LCYC.3.1.1]: a cache write whose product no rule of the SCC consumes does not stop the SCC being admitted. Rule `r` matches a `Trig`, writes `cache key: "k"` and withdraws its match, a one-rule SCC through its own withdraw edge ([LCYC.3.2.2]). No schema is emitted, and no rule of the SCC reads `cached()`, so the SCC is admitted and the program compiles. PATH PINNED: `dsc.cycle.lcyc_3_1_1_consumes_cache` finding a write and no read. Twin: LCYC.3.1.1_scc_reads_its_cache_write_refused, which adds the `cached("k")` read and is refused; a check that refused every SCC carrying a `cache` would refuse this one too.
rules_ds:
schema Trig scope explicit:
    v: Int

rule r:
    Trig t
->
    cache key: "k" value: t.v
    withdraw t
